routes.name: Interest Free Student Loan Scheme (IFSLS) - 11th intake, academic year 2026/27
routes.provider: Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education (Higher Education Division), Student Loans Scheme Division
routes.provider_type: state scheme (loan for approved non-state degree programmes)
routes.duration: Loan period 12 years: 3 or 4 year degree + 1 year grace + 8 years (96 instalments, 3-yr degree) or 7 years (84 instalments, 4-yr degree) repayment
routes.intake_timing: 11th intake (2026/27): online applications 17.08.2026 to 12:00 midnight 27.09.2026 (CLOSED); online interviews 15.10.2026-19.11.2026 via Microsoft Teams; registration at institutes January-February 2027. Appeals window: one month from publication of selection results.
routes.entry_requirements_text: The candidates who have passed G.C.E (A/L) Examination in 2023, 2024 and 2025 conducted by the Department of Examinations in Sri Lanka and have been considered as qualified for university entrance are entitled to apply for IFSLS for the academic year 2026/27, subject to following conditions; (i) Having obtained simple (S) passes for all the three subjects in one and the same sitting and not exceeding three sittings, and (ii) Having a minimum of 30 marks for the Common General Test at any sitting without exceeding three sittings (The result must be obtained at the time of interviews conducted), and (iii) Minimum of simple (S) pass for General English at the G.C.E (A/L) Examination or Minimum of simple (S) pass for English Language at the G.C.E (O/L) Examination, and (iv) The age of the candidates should be 25 years or below by 27th September, 2026.
routes.source_locator: Student Handbook IFSLS, Section 1.2 (p.5), 1.3-1.7 (pp.6-13); timing from sources/ifsl_faq.html and sources/ifsl_home.html; handbook link page sources/ifsl_guidebook.html; division functions sources/mohe_student_loan_division.html; conflicting older page sources/mohe_loan_overview.html
routes.notes: Approved institutes for 11th intake: Handbook section 1.4 lists 17 (SLIIT [Malabe, Matara, Kandy, Jaffna], NSBM, CINEC, SIBA, ICASL, HORIZON, KIU, SLTC, SAEGIS, ESOFT, ICHEM, ICBT [Colombo, Kandy], BCI, NIIBS, BMS, LYC, SLITA). CONFLICT: the FAQ page says 'sixteen approved' NSHEIs (its table omits SLITA); the MOHE 'Overview of Student Loan' page says 16 but lists 18 (adds Gateway College) and still cites A/L 2022-2024 (outdated). Students pay only the scheme course fee stated in the handbook, plus their own repeat-exam and bridging-course costs. Must get at least C for every compulsory subject and 80% attendance. No household-income eligibility condition was found in the official handbook or FAQ. Next intake (12th) dates not published as of retrieval.

Shall have passed the G.C.E Advanced Level Examination with a minimum of three S passes. (Can vary according to the scholarship program). Shall not be an individual who has registered as an internal student to pursue a degree program at a state university coming under the purview of the University Grants Commission. English language competency (This will be determined as per the language medium of the scholarship award) Shall be in good physical health.

routes.entry_requirements_text: 1.2 Minimum requirements for university admission Candidates who are pronounced eligible for university admission by the Commissioner General of Examinations should have obtained; (a) At least ‘S’ grades in all three approved subjects in one sitting, within a maximum of three attempts. (b) A minimum mark of 30% for the Common General Paper ... Candidates who have not obtained a minimum of 30% shall re-sit and obtain a minimum of 30% for the common general paper in a next available year within three attempts allowed for university admission, to be eligible to get registered for the courses of study of the universities for which the candidates have already been selected based on Z Score, in a future academic year. ... 1.7 ... 1. Students who sat the G.C.E. (Advanced Level) Examination on more than three (03) occasions. Students need not sit the examination consecutively, but once the three attempts are completed, the student becomes ineligible to apply on the results of the subsequent attempts or on the results of the previous attempts.

routes.notes: A third attempt uses up eligibility: the app must count prior sittings and warn that a 3rd sitting forecloses using earlier results. 'To be fair to all, opportunity to enter into a free state sponsored course of study is given only once.' (handbook 1.3). Private-candidate procedure and fees: not found.
